entries.name: Common vampire bat
behaviour: feeds on sleeping mammals, using razor incisors and an anticoagulant saliva
grooms companions and shares food, the only bat known to share blood meals
prefers livestock near forest edges; a nuisance and a rabies risk where cattle meet jungle
entries.notes: The face of every vampire story; handle dead specimens with care, they can carry rabies.

entries.name: Seba's short-tailed fruit bat
behaviour: roosts under bridges, hollows and foliage in colonies of 5 to 200
key seed disperser of Piper shrubs; carries fruit to a feeding roost and spits the seeds
the bat you actually see when a torch sweeps a ceiling
entries.notes: The commonest bat of the Neotropics; thick fur, stubby tail, important janitor of the forest floor's seed rain.

entries.name: Pygmy marmoset
behaviour: world's smallest monkey; calls sound like insect chirps
family groups of 2 to 9; one breeding pair, helpers raise the twins
gouges holes in gum trees and farms the sap that oozes out
entries.notes: A pocket-sized monkey that gnaws sap holes like a beetle; the size of a small rat, twice as opinionated.

entries.name: Common squirrel monkey
behaviour: troops of 20 to 75 typically, fission-fusion splits up to 500 for a fig feast
males have black muzzles and white eye rings; in season, swell to twice normal bulk
hearty, curious, and bold around lodge dining decks with tourists

voxel_model.pattern: white mask, black muzzle, golden back

entries.notes: The consummate rainforest monkey: hyperactive, social, and utterly unafraid of the lodge rail.

entries.name: Three-striped night monkey
behaviour: the only truly nocturnal monkey; enormous round eyes, no colour vision to speak of
monogamous pairs share infant care; the male carries the baby by day
hides under tree holes and vine curtains; a shape of darkness with two reflective garnet eyes

voxel_model.pattern: three dark crown stripes and a face mask

entries.notes: A little owl that is actually a monkey; one of the eeriest paired eye-shines in a night walk.

entries.name: Central American agouti
behaviour: stands upright like a tiny kangaroo to inspect threats, then launches away
caches thousands of palm nuts; buried seeds it forgets become new trees
cuts open hard palm nuts holding them between its feet like a squirrel

voxel_model.pattern: reddish rump over a dark grizzled body

entries.notes: The forest's planter: agouti caches drive mahogany and palm regeneration; losing them hollows out the forest.

entries.name: Northern tamandua
behaviour: rips open termite mounds with huge hooked claws, then vacuums up the interior with a 40 cm tongue
prehensile tail works as a fifth limb in the lower canopy
when cornered hisses like a snake and slashes with both forelimbs
entries.notes: Half anteater, half fire alarm; a good hiss and a sight you will not forget quickly.

entries.name: Slow loris
behaviour: the only venomous primate: elbow gland toxin plus a bite wounds slowly and festers
hand-over-hand climber, faster on a careful branch than a human expects
freezes perfectly still when alarmed; those eyes refuse to be out-stared

voxel_model.pattern: white face with dark eye stripe, wet nose

entries.notes: Weaponised with a surprise cocktail; poaching for the pet trade has pushed it toward oblivion.

entries.name: Aye-aye
behaviour: skeletal middle finger taps wood to locate grubs, then tears them out with the same finger
rodent-like incisors grow forever; gnaws a perfect round hole to reach the cavity
Madagascar's living ghost story; locally tabooed as an omen of death

voxel_model.pattern: pale ears and wild skeletal finger

entries.notes: Endangered and irreplaceable: the strangest animal alive and the reason Madagascar feels like another planet.

entries.name: Philippine tarsier
behaviour: eyes larger than its brain; fixed staring orbs that do not rotate
head twists nearly 180 degrees to hear and spot prey in the dark
leaps between saplings in 3 m bounds; cannot survive long in a cage

voxel_model.pattern: giant golden eyes with black starbursts

entries.notes: A palm-sized primate with carnival-mirror eyes; nearly impossible to keep alive, so look, don't touch.

entries.name: Rufous-tailed hummingbird
behaviour: hovers motionless at flowers, wings a blur, tail a rufous fan
hyperactive defender of flower patches, chasing off much bigger birds
sips insects mid-air for protein; a ruby-and-emerald helicopter
entries.notes: The blur at the feeder: hummingbirds burn food faster than any vertebrate on the planet.

entries.name: Green-rumped parrotlet
behaviour: a green sparrow-sized parrot that travels in chattering, tumbling flocks
roosts and nests in old woodpecker holes, termites nests and fence posts
males flash cobalt wing patches in flight; otherwise impeccably subtle
entries.notes: The parrot's pocket edition; a joy to keep and a common sight at tropical feeders.

entries.name: Collared aracari
behaviour: travels in comical flocks of 6 to 12, bill bouncing in flight
bill edged like a butter knife; grabs fruit, tosses back the head and swallows whole
radiates yellow and scarlet from the nest hole in a red-breasted vest

voxel_model.pattern: yellow cheek, red belly band, pale bill with black tip

entries.notes: The mini-toucan that gathers fruit with a serrated beak; loud, gregarious, impossible to ignore.

entries.name: Golden-headed toucanet
behaviour: a dark midstory specialist of the Brazilian Atlantic forest
sexes look different: males bright gold-capped, females deep green with chestnut cheeks
clings beneath branches while plucking fruit, slow and deliberate
entries.notes: A tiny toucanet for quiet cathedrals of Atlantic forest; heard far more often than seen.

entries.name: Turquoise-browed motmot
behaviour: racket-tipped tail swings like a pendulum on a string
beats prey senselessly on a branch before swallowing it
perches dead-still scanning for movement; national bird of Nicaragua
entries.notes: The pendulum-bird: a lazy-eyed feline impostor that hunts snakes from a fence post.

entries.name: Oriental pied hornbill
behaviour: female seals herself inside the nest hole with mud, fed through a narrow slit by the male
hammering bill and whooshing wingbeats herald a hornbill before it is seen
hornbills disperse giant fruit trees across South and Southeast Asia
entries.notes: A cattle-sized flying commitment to monogamy; one of the loud announcements of Asian forest dawns.

entries.name: Tokay gecko
behaviour: barks its own name: 'to-kay, to-kay' rings across the rooftops all night
velvety scales and lamellae let it walk up any wall, upside down included
flashy but vicious; a big one draws blood with a single bite and never lets go
entries.notes: The house guardian of Southeast Asia; half pet deterrent, half intruder, all audacity.

entries.name: Green basilisk
behaviour: runs bipedally across water for several metres, slapping with expanded hind feet
males bear a leathery casque and crest; females greener and crestless
freezes as a green statue when spotted, then bolts for the water
entries.notes: The so-called 'Jesus Christ lizard': a happy parasol of green above the river stones.

entries.name: Eyelash viper
behaviour: supracanthal scales jut over each eye like false eyelashes
ambush predator of low branches; strikes with hemotoxic venom at the first warm animal to pass
forms exist in gold, brown, peach and emerald; a snake-shop staple and a leading cause of snakebite tourism

voxel_model.pattern: eyelash scales; yellow, brown or emerald morphs

entries.notes: A plated jewel with a bad temper; the most photogenic snake in the canopy and the reason night walks have rules.

entries.name: Satanic leaf-tailed gecko
behaviour: flattens against a mossy branch and becomes a dead leaf, veins, rime and bite-marks included
leaps with rocketing legs, lands thuddingly like a falling leaf
drops its tail voluntarily when grabbed; tail mocks a waving insect

voxel_model.pattern: leaf mimicry with notched tail and lichen flecks

entries.notes: The gecko that disproves the idea that leaves are plant organs; collectors fly across oceans for this one.

entries.name: Oriental garden lizard
behaviour: breeding males flush brick-red from head to shoulder; the rest are green to bronze
perches upright like a tiny dragon, fanning the fan-shaped urban lizard look
ubiquitous on walls, fences and roadside hotels across South and Southeast Asia
entries.notes: The garden sentry of Asia: sun-up, head-bobbing, impossible not to notice.

entries.name: Golden poison frog
behaviour: skin carries batrachotoxin: enough to kill ten grown men from a pinprick
Chocó peoples once tipped blowgun darts on captive frogs
captive-born frogs are harmless; toxin comes from wild alkaloid-laden prey
entries.notes: The most toxic animal on Earth; the little yellow beacon that taught the world to respect small things.

entries.name: Fleischman's glass frog
behaviour: translucent belly skin: you can read the numbers on a spring balance through it
females lay eggs on the undersides of leaves over rainforest streams
males guard the egg clutch and keep it moist until the tadpoles drop into water
entries.notes: A frog with a window where its stomach should be; one of the first amphibians to seduce nature-film crews.

entries.name: Wallace's flying frog
behaviour: spreads huge webbed feet and parachutes 10 m or more between canopy trees
pale flank flash marks show in flight; disappears as soon as it lands
builds a foamy nest of several hundred eggs on a leaf over a pond; rain dissolves the foam and the tadpoles drop in

voxel_model.pattern: giant glider feet with flank stripes

entries.notes: A green parachute with a heartbeat; named by Wallace himself on the Malay Archipelago.

entries.name: Spotted stream frog
behaviour: flashes huge webbed feet in a slow, rhythmic wave to signal across the white noise of waterfalls
males own a boulder and defend it with foot-flags and klik calls
a Singapore and Malaya speciality of boulder-strewn rainforest streams

voxel_model.pattern: webbed foot flags and speckled flanks

entries.notes: The semaphore frog: it cannot afford to be heard, so it has learned to wave instead.

entries.name: Cardinal tetra
behaviour: shoals of hundreds move as one flickering neon ribbon through blackwater streams
an unbroken red stripe below an electric-blue band from nose to tail
the aquarium trade's most familiar Amazon export

voxel_model.pattern: electric blue and true-red longitudinal stripe

entries.notes: The little neon comma of the Rio Negro; one handful of water carries a hundred.

entries.name: Clown pleco
behaviour: rasps lignin and biofilm off driftwood with a spoon-shaped mouth
bold black-and-white barred flag of a fish, funnel-deep pelvic fins
cave-spawner; a treasured oddball of the aquarium hobby

voxel_model.pattern: bold black and white zebra bars

entries.notes: The only fish that insists on eating furniture; if you put down driftwood, this is what's going to notice.

entries.name: Freshwater angelfish
behaviour: tall sickle-shaped fins and vertical bars make it a living silhouette among the roots
monogamous pairs clean a leaf face and tank-guard their glassy fry
a staple of every home aquarium, wild and marbled varieties alike
entries.notes: The living valentine slipping between mangrove roots; a pet-shop icon straight from the Amazon.

entries.name: Atlas moth
behaviour: one of the world's largest moths, wingspan beyond 25 cm
wingtips curled and patterned to mimic a cobra head; lizards and birds keep their distance
adults do not feed at all; they live on stored fat for a fortnight and find a mate
entries.notes: A sheet of autumn that flew; the adult's entire job is to find another of its kind before dawn.

entries.name: Hercules beetle
behaviour: males carry two enormous horns for prying rivals off branches
relative to its own weight, among the strongest animals ever recorded
grubs need years in a rotting log; adults live just months on sap
entries.notes: The heavyweight champion of the beetle world; drop one and the light undergrowth quakes.

entries.name: Emperor blue morpho
behaviour: iridescence is diffraction, not pigment; close the wings and the blue vanishes to brown
a male's flash is visible a hundred metres off through canopy gaps
hindwing eyespots startle attackers who miss the escape flutter

voxel_model.pattern: electric blue upper wings, eyespots below

entries.notes: The single brightest thing flying in the understory; the forest's travelling blue flame.

entries.name: Orchid mantis
behaviour: mimics an orchid so completely that bees fly in to pollinate it
legs feathered like petal lobes; sways in the breeze like a flower
females 2x larger than males; cannibalism the norm after mating
entries.notes: The flower that eats its pollinators; a collector's holy grail and a genuine horror story for insects.

entries.name: Bullet ant
behaviour: Schmidt sting index 4+: 24 hours of full-body paralysis from one hit
colonies of up to 1000 workers nest at the bases of emergent canopy trees
Satere-Mawe warriors wear gloves filled with stinging bullet ants as a coming-of-age ordeal
entries.notes: The most painful sting in the insect world; the forest floor's fuse is lit at all times.

entries.name: Army ant
entries.migrates: nomadic swarm bivouacking, never settling longer than about 20 days
behaviour: a moving wall of up to 700,000 workers, a living storm that sweeps a 100 m front
no fixed nest: at night the workers link limbs into a breathing ball around the queen
antbirds shadow the raid, picking off the fleeing survivors

voxel_model.pattern: orange head on a dark body

entries.notes: The parade that eats anything that cannot fly or burrow; a single raid clears the forest floor for weeks.

entries.name: Golden silk orb-weaver
behaviour: silk is hauled in by weavers for fabric; golden strands glint like metal in sunlight
males are tiny dwarfs that live permanently at the margins of a female's web
a full orb web is a foot across; birds tear the webs apart just to collect the golden threads
entries.notes: Spins fabric warmer and stronger than steel by weight; the spider that weaves sunlight.

entries.name: Brazilian wandering spider
behaviour: hunts on the ground at night with no web; legspan up to 30 cm, body 5 cm
waves and erects its front legs when threatened, like a boxer guarding its face
hitchhikes in banana shipments; this is the 'banana spider' of legend

voxel_model.pattern: grey-brown with hairy legs, red chelicerae flash

entries.notes: The most dangerous spider in the Americas; fast, big-mouthed and nomadic. Shake the bananas out over the sink.

entries.name: Amazonian whip spider
behaviour: not a spider: an amblypygid, the tailless whip scorpion
no venom, no silk; hunts with raptorial spined pedipalps and reads air with a whip-like first leg pair
females carry eggs in a sac and then the spiderlings on their backs
entries.notes: A shadow wearing six legs and two antennas; scary-looking, harmless, and beloved by exotic pet keepers.

entries.name: Giant African snail
behaviour: can self-fertilise and lay 100 to 400 eggs per clutch, several clutches a year
one of the world's worst invasive species; eats crops and lime mortar alike
intermediate host of rat lungworm, a serious human parasite
entries.notes: The escape artist farm snail that ate its way across the tropics; never knowingly release one.

entries.name: Red land crab
entries.migrates: en masse to the coast to spawn, triggered by the first heavy rains
behaviour: crimson carapace the colour of a warning sign; claws darker still
once a year the whole coast erupts into a crawling red tide marching to the sea
females release larvae into the surf on lunar tides; adults return to the forest
entries.notes: The red army of the Costa Rican and Nicaraguan coasts; roads close for their march to the sea.
